citations.narrative:
The facility has exceeded the maximum number of animals allowed on their license without prior authorization. The
license has authorized up to 850 animals. The routine inspection conducted on 01-September-2026 identified that the
facility currently houses approximately 1110 animals. The USDA license authorizes a specific number of animals to
ensure that the facility and personnel possess adequate facilities, employees and knowledge to provide sufficient
husbandry to the regulated animals. The number and severity of the non-compliances documented on the routine
inspection report demonstrates that exceeding the approved animal numbers has resulted in the facilities inability to
properly care for the animal causing serious welfare concerns.
The facility must obtain authorization to increase the approved maximum number of animals or reduce the number of
regulated animals to a number which is under the maximum threshold authorized under the current license. Correct
by,16-September-2026.

There is an insufficient number of adequately trained employees to carry out the level of husbandry practices and care
required by the Animal Welfare Act. There is one full-time employee, one full-time assistant, and a part-time assistant
responsible for the care of approximately 1110 animals at this facility. There is a history of numerous and severe non-
compliances identified pertaining to the cleaning, sanitation, watering, and veterinary care.
The issues seen are consistent with shortages of personnel. Insufficient personnel can lead to a failure in maintenance of
the facility, delayed care for the animals, and unnecessary suffering and health concerns for the animals. The facility must
ensure a sufficient number of adequately trained employees are utilized to maintain the professionally acceptable level of
husbandry practices set forth in this subpart. Such practices shall be under the supervision of an animal caretaker who
has a background in animal husbandry or care.
Physical inspection of the facility was conducted on 01-September-2026
This inspection report is a continuation based on those inspection findings.
The review of the inspection report and exit interview were conducted on 02-September-2026 with a Facility
Representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
